subject: Compact SKU packaging and channel float for AWS private offer
messages:
From: Lila Patel <lila.patel@amazon.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compact SKU packaging + channel-float suggestion for Everwell private offer

Hi Priyom / Ben —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. I pulled a compact SKU proposal together for the Everwell PoC and wanted to float an option that could help preserve channel economics while giving the customer a simplified buying experience. See attached: compact-sku-proposal.pdf (two-page summary + pricing waterfall).

High-level idea:
- Offer a single metered SKU that covers core inference and a modest premium for managed features.
- List price set to match equivalent on-demand units; private-offer discount applied at offer creation to hit committed ARR target.
- Channel float: allow a transient channel margin top-up for the first 3 months (to cover reseller onboarding) that steps down as usage stabilizes.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you confirm whether an initial 12% channel float (applied outside the private-offer discount layer) is operationally feasible for you?
2) Do you have constraints on invoicing / true-up timing for that float?
3) Any objection to a 30-day true-up cadence for this customer?

If helpful I'd like to book a 30-min sync tomorrow to run through the waterfall and pass-through mechanics.

Cheers,
Lila
Lila Patel | AWS Account Manager, Marketplace
AWS Marketplace

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 11:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Compact SKU packaging + channel-float suggestion for Everwell private offer

Lila —

Appreciate the deck, quick read looks reasonable. A few upfront notes:
- We can support a transient channel top-up but need to pin the mechanics (is it a separate line item the reseller invoices, or embedded in the offer as a settlement?); that affects revenue recognition and tax treatment.
- 12% seems a bit high for a short pilot; can you share the rationale? If it's to offset reseller implementation costs, a 6–8% onboarding uplift might be sufficient.
- 30-day true-up is preferable from our ops side (helps with metering alignment). Anything shorter increases reconciliation complexity.

Ben — looping you in to model the margin pass-through and confirm what floor we need to protect Redwood unit economics.

If you and Ben are free tomorrow 10am PT, let's take Lila up on the sync.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das | Head of Marketplace GTM, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lila Patel <lila.patel@amazon.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:30:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Compact SKU packaging + channel-float suggestion for Everwell private offer

Thanks for the note and the proposal, Lila — good starting point. Quick margin read below:

- Assumptions I used: list price = $0.020 per inference-unit, expected steady-state customer usage = 18M units/month, 3-month onboarding spike = +40% usage.
- If we apply a 12% float outside the private-offer discount, Redwood net goes down by ~9.8% at steady-state once reseller take is included. That's probably too aggressive for a pilot.

Proposed path:
1) Pilot channel float = 7% for months 1–3, payable as an off-invoice settlement to reseller (keeps the private-offer discount clean).
2) Add a 10% floor on combined Redwood net after pass-through (so if the gross math would push us below floor we automatically reduce float).
3) 30-day true-up cadence and a 60-day invoice holdback to allow meter corrections before settlement.

Operational asks from marketplace / finance:
- We'll need a margin-model spreadsheet to validate the pass-through (I attached margin-model.xlsx).
- Confirm whether AWS can surface a separate settlement line in their billing (preferred) vs. embedding in the private-offer negative line item. Separate settlement simplifies GL mapping.

If everyone agrees, I support the pilot with the 7% onboarding float + 10% floor.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: margin-model.xlsx
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Lila Patel <lila.patel@amazon.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compact SKU packaging + channel-float suggestion for Everwell private offer

Folks —

From a marketplace-ops and legal/recognition perspective a couple of constraints to call out before we lock anything in:

1) Invoicing and recognition: a separate off-invoice settlement to the reseller is fine, but Redwood requires the settlement terms in the private offer contract appendix and the reseller must sign a reseller pass-through agreement. That ensures we don't have deferred revenue leakage.
2) True-up timing: 30-day true-up is acceptable; ops prefers explicit meter-exception windows to be +/- 10% for the first 90 days to reduce noisy corrections.
3) Pilot SKU approach: recommend we create a 'compact-pilot-v1' SKU with a 90-day canary period, restrict private-offer quantity cap to 80% of expected steady-state, and then auto-scale the SKU to full capacity after a signed operational review. This reduces billing surprises.

Action items:
- AWS: can you confirm whether the reseller settlement will be a separate billing line and provide a sample settlement statement? (Lila)
- AWS & Redwood Sales: agree to pilot parameters and get sign-off from Everwell procurement on the 90-day canary and 30-day true-up.
- Redwood Finance: I'll run the margin model and return a signed internal authorization; Ben, please flag any tax/regulatory implications in the EU if this customer expands there.

I placed a HubSpot note under the deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4831) and created an internal ops checklist. Once we have the sample settlement statement from AWS we'll draft the private-offer appendix and reseller pass-through.

Irene Choi | Marketplace Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
